physiology:
The traditions seat this code in the spleen, the body's quiet keeper of memory and threat. It is the organ that remembers who you have already met, which fevers you have already survived, which intrusions are friend and which are enemy. It keeps a long ledger written in cells, and it reads the world by that ledger before the mind has any opinion at all.

The shadow has its bodily floor here. The old fear of being cut off from the tribe runs in the immune memory, and when it fires it does not feel like a thought, it feels like a low alarm under the ribs that never quite goes off. The body is scanning, sorting, deciding what is safe to let in. Money, status, the pile of belongings, all of it the spleen has been roped into defending as if it were the warmth of the winter fire. It is exhausting to be on guard at that level for a life.

The climb is also bodily. The alarm quiets when the body senses it belongs to something older than its own skin. Breath gets longer. The grip in the gut loosens. There is a softening at the back of the throat that comes before any decision is made. The instinct stops scanning for threat and starts reading time, the slow shape of what is worth keeping, what is ready to fall away. The body remembers it is part of a chain, and the chain has been holding.
amino_acid:
Deeper than the organ, this code answers to a single amino acid, aspartic acid. It is one of the messengers the nervous system uses to pass a signal across the gap between cells, the chemistry of a body that is paying attention. It is also one of the building blocks the body can make for itself, woven directly into the cycle by which old proteins are broken down and remade into new ones.

There is a teaching in that. The code about preservation, about what to keep alive and what to let rot, runs on the very chemistry by which the body decides the same thing for itself, moment by moment, without ever asking. The cells take apart what is finished with. They keep the nitrogen, the carbon, the parts still good. They build the next thing from what the last thing was. The card is named in the body before any human ever names it. What you call the art of grafting, your chemistry has been doing under the skin for as long as you have been alive.
